layoutData.tagline: Leading HVAC and Plumbing Service Provider with 2,900 Recurring Members

layoutData.body:
Lakeshore Home Comfort Ltd. has served the Hamilton and Burlington, Ontario area for 27 years. The business was established in 1998 as an independent heating and cooling service company, operating initially as a sole proprietorship under the name Moretti Heating. In March 2004, owner Anthony (Tony) Moretti incorporated the business as Lakeshore Home Comfort Ltd., the name chosen by his wife Maria.

From the beginning, the company has maintained the same phone number—a point of pride that reflects the continuity and trust the business has built in the community. That phone line has been answered without interruption since 2004.

The business provides comprehensive residential HVAC and plumbing services. The HVAC side encompasses system installations (furnaces, air conditioners, heat pumps), preventive maintenance through the Comfort Club membership program, emergency repairs, and indoor air quality products. The plumbing division handles service calls, drain work, and water heater installations. In 2011, Lakeshore became a Northaire Premier Dealer, a relationship that continues to provide extended warranty coverage and preferred pricing on equipment.

In 2018, the company moved into its current 14,000 square foot facility on Bayfront Commerce Drive in Hamilton and signed a long-term lease to support continued growth. The following year, the business transitioned its operations to cloud-based software, modernizing dispatch, invoicing, and customer management.

Today, Lakeshore Home Comfort operates 24 service vans and employs 36 people, including 24 licensed technicians in the field. The company has built a base of approximately 6,800 active customers and maintains 2,900 Comfort Club members who rely on the business for year-round service and priority response.

Tony Moretti has led the business since its founding. Under his ownership, Lakeshore has never laid off staff—not during the 2009 recession and not during COVID-19. The company pulls permits on every installation, registers every warranty, and keeps all revenue on the books. Everything is done by the book, a principle that has shaped the company's reputation and its relationships with customers, suppliers, and regulators.

layoutData.description: The Comfort Club maintenance-plan membership program is a cornerstone of Lakeshore Home Comfort's recurring revenue model and competitive advantage. As of March 31, 2025, the company has 2,900 active members (1,972 Silver, 928 Gold) generating $910,020 in annual recurring revenue. Members receive two precision tune-ups per year, priority scheduling, discounts on repairs, and no diagnostic fees. Gold members also receive an annual plumbing inspection and water heater flush, no after-hours or weekend surcharges, and higher repair discounts. The program has grown from just 140 members in 2012 to its current base through consistent enrollment at every installation (approximately one in four install customers join) and active renewal management. Churn is low at 85 to 90 percent annual renewal, with cancellations primarily due to customers moving or selling their homes. Members provide a steady pipeline of replacement equipment sales, as they call Lakeshore first when their systems fail. Approximately 400 to 500 new members are added annually, offsetting natural attrition and driving net growth. The membership base is a key driver of the company's resilient financial performance and customer retention.

left.title: Customer Profile
left.content:
Lakeshore Home Comfort serves approximately 6,800 unique customers annually, invoiced in 2024. The customer base is overwhelmingly residential, consisting of homeowners in Hamilton, Burlington, Stoney Creek, Ancaster, Dundas, Waterdown, and Grimsby.

The largest customer is Quillmont Property Management, which accounts for approximately $150,000 in annual revenue across roughly 40 rental properties. The relationship dates to approximately 2016-17 and covers both HVAC and plumbing services under a year-to-year service agreement that auto-renews with approximately 60 days cancellation notice. Payment terms extend to 45-60 days.

No single customer represents more than 5 percent of total revenue. The business also serves property management companies, co-ops, and maintains one builder relationship. Builder work has been selectively turned down due to capacity constraints — approximately $300,000 in new-build work was declined in 2024 for lack of available technicians.

Repeat customers and referrals represent approximately 50 percent of new business annually. The Comfort Club membership base of 2,900 active members provides a stable foundation of recurring revenue and drives equipment replacement opportunities when member systems reach end of life.

items.title: Comfort Club Membership Expansion
items.description: The Comfort Club has grown from 140 members in 2012 to 2,900 active members at March 31, 2025, generating $910,000 in annual recurring revenue. Significant untapped potential exists in adjacent markets: 60+ members already in Oakville without active marketing. Geographic expansion into Oakville and Milton represents a natural growth path, leveraging the existing brand reputation and referral network to capture new recurring revenue streams and equipment replacement opportunities.

items.title: Commercial HVAC Services
items.description: The company currently serves a small commercial segment with rooftop unit maintenance, primarily through technician Luis Fernandes who handles some rooftop work. This represents an underdeveloped revenue channel. Expanding commercial service offerings and building a dedicated commercial maintenance portfolio would diversify the customer base and create additional recurring revenue beyond the residential Comfort Club program.

items.title: Water Heater and Equipment Rental Program
items.description: Approximately 300 water heaters are installed annually and sold outright. A rental program at $25-35 per month per unit would build a substantial recurring revenue base comparable to the Comfort Club model. Furnace and air conditioner rentals represent additional opportunities. This growth path requires upfront capital investment and long-term commitment but offers high-margin, predictable cash flow once the rental base is established.

items.title: Electrical Licensing and Panel Upgrade Services
items.description: Heat pump installations represent approximately 25-28% of install revenue (roughly $1 million annually), with 70-75% of heat pump jobs requiring electrical panel upgrades from 100-amp to 200-amp service. These upgrades currently add $1,500-2,000 per job and are subcontracted to Voltmere Electric Ltd. Obtaining an Electrical Safety Authority (ESA) contractor licence and bringing this work in-house would capture the panel upgrade margin, simplify the customer experience with a single point of contact, and reduce scheduling dependencies on third-party subcontractors.

items.title: New Construction and Builder Relationships
items.description: The company turned down approximately $300,000 of new-build HVAC work in 2024 due to lack of available technicians. Builder relationships represent a largely untapped channel that could provide predictable project pipelines and volume equipment purchasing leverage. With additional technician capacity, this segment offers significant incremental revenue without the marketing acquisition costs associated with residential service work.

items.title: Additional Technician Hiring
items.description: Labour availability is the primary constraint on growth. Three technician positions have been open since January 2025, with the company receiving applications but struggling to find qualified candidates. Management estimates that additional technicians would enable $500,000-1,000,000 in incremental annual revenue. Current demand exceeds technician capacity across all service lines. Solving the hiring challenge through competitive compensation, apprenticeship programs, or acquisitions of smaller shops for their labour would unlock immediate top-line growth.

items.title: Qualified Technician Shortage
items.description: Three open positions since January 2025; receiving applications but struggling to find qualified candidates. Industry-wide shortage of licensed HVAC and plumbing technicians constrains growth. Additional techs would enable $500,000 to $1,000,000 incremental revenue. Company pays competitively to retain skilled staff.

items.title: Government Rebate Program Dependency
items.description: Heat pump business heavily dependent on government rebates — phones ring when rebates are available, goes quiet for a month when programs change (every year and a half). Approximately 95 heat pump installations in 2024 at $11,000 to $12,000 each (roughly $1,050,000 to $1,140,000 in heat pump revenue). Rebate program changes create uncertainty and temporary slowdowns.

items.title: Supplier Concentration
items.description: 55% of equipment and material purchases from one distributor (Kestrel Bay HVAC Supply Inc.). Long-standing 20-year relationship with approximately $60,000 annual volume rebate tied to purchasing volume. Buyer must invest in relationship handoff early to maintain pricing and rebate structure.

items.title: Weather Variability
items.description: Seasonal weather patterns directly impact revenue. Cool July 2023 hurt air conditioning business and impacted revenue for that month. Heating season and summer heat waves are critical demand periods. Comfort Club membership base provides stability against weather swings.

items.title: Electrical Subcontractor Dependency
items.description: Voltmere Electric Ltd. is the sole electrical subcontractor for heat pump panel upgrades (approximately 70 jobs per year; 70 to 75% of heat pump jobs require panel upgrades). No electrical contractor licence in-house, so scheduling depends on Voltmere capacity. Switching subcontractors would take time and could raise costs.

If owner exits, buyer needs to add a new G1 certificate holder or rely on Dave staying. Registration renews in November.

layoutData.body:
The seller has committed to a comprehensive six-month full-time transition to ensure continuity and a smooth handover to the new owner. Tony Moretti will remain actively involved through the critical heating season, guiding the buyer through the busiest operational period and facilitating the transfer of key supplier relationships, customer connections, and operational knowledge.

The transition plan is structured around a closing timeline designed to minimize disruption. The seller prefers to close by early 2026, deliberately avoiding the mid-July peak busy season when the business is at maximum capacity and management bandwidth is stretched. This timing allows the new owner to onboard during a more manageable period and build confidence before entering the next high-demand cycle.

During the six-month transition, Tony will bring comfort advisor Steve Marchetti to referral sales calls where customers specifically request the owner. By the end of the transition period, customers will naturally ask for Steve by name. Steve and Laura Kim, the two comfort advisors, are fully capable of handling the approximately 60 to 70 referral sales jobs Tony currently closes each year, which represent roughly 15 percent of total installations at a higher dollar amount.

The business is designed to operate with minimal owner dependency. Dave Kowalczyk (Service Manager), Denise Tran (Office Manager and Bookkeeper), and Kevin O'Brien (Installation Manager) manage daily operations, dispatch, technician scheduling, installation logistics, payroll, accounts payable and receivable, and month-end close. Tony's role centers on being the face of the company, handling pricing strategy, managing supplier relationships, and closing select high-value sales. The transition will systematically transfer these responsibilities to the buyer and the existing management team.

Tony has indicated he will provide whatever ongoing phone support the buyer needs after the formal transition period ends, emphasizing his commitment to doing it right and ensuring the long-term success of the business under new ownership.

layoutData.body:
After 27 years building and operating Lakeshore Home Comfort, Anthony (Tony) Moretti has decided to retire and relocate to Florida.

Tony founded the business in 1998 as an independent HVAC contractor and incorporated it in 2004. Over more than two decades, he has grown the company from a small service operation into a full-service HVAC and plumbing business serving the Hamilton and Burlington area. The company now employs 36 people, operates 24 service vans, and serves approximately 6,800 customers annually.

The business has been built on a foundation of quality work, fair pricing, and treating customers and employees well. Tony has maintained the same phone number since 2004, pulled permits on every job, and kept everything on the books. The company has never laid off staff—not during the 2009 recession and not during COVID.

Tony's decision to sell is driven purely by personal plans for retirement. The business is performing well, with revenue reaching $7,412,000 in fiscal 2024 and continuing to grow in early 2025. The management team of Dave Kowalczyk, Denise Tran, and Kevin O'Brien runs daily operations, and the technician base is stable and experienced.

Tony is committed to a successful transition. He will provide six months of full-time support to the buyer, remaining present through the heating season to help transfer supplier relationships, customer connections, and operational knowledge. He will continue to be available by phone after the formal transition period to ensure the buyer's success.

Tony's priority is finding a buyer who will treat the team well and continue to invest in the business's growth.
layoutData.pullQuote: I didn't build this business to flip it. I built it to last. I want someone who's going to take care of the people here—they've taken care of me for years.

items.title: Commitment to Team & Culture
items.description: The seller seeks a buyer who will treat the team well and not view employees as a spreadsheet. Lakeshore Home Comfort has never laid off staff — not during the 2009 recession and not during COVID — and has built a culture of stability with many technicians serving 10 to 16 years. Retention agreements for 2 to 3 key people at closing are recommended, particularly for Dave Kowalczyk (Service Manager).

items.title: Growth Investment Mindset
items.description: The ideal buyer is willing to invest in the untapped growth opportunities that the retiring owner has not pursued: water heater and HVAC equipment rental programs (recurring revenue at $25 to $35 per month), obtaining an electrical contractor licence to capture panel upgrade margin currently subcontracted, expanding the Comfort Club membership base into Oakville and Milton where 60+ members already exist without active marketing, developing commercial rooftop unit maintenance work, and hiring additional technicians to capture the $500,000 to $1,000,000 in incremental revenue currently constrained by labour capacity.

items.title: HVAC or Home Services Operator
items.description: A buyer with existing HVAC, plumbing, or home services operations will recognize the value of the 2,900-member Comfort Club recurring revenue base, the fully licensed technician team, and the Northaire Premier Dealer status. Experience in managing service fleets, dispatch operations, and trade licensing requirements in Ontario will ease the transition and preserve the operational momentum the management team has built.

items.title: Non-Compete Agreement
items.description: Tony Moretti will sign a 5-year non-compete covering a 100-kilometre radius from Hamilton, or whatever terms the buyer requires. Tony is not opening a competing business and is committed to ensuring a clean handoff.
